create.title: Create new scale user
create.description: Home Assistant creates the scale user on the scale and chooses its consent code itself. The scale uses the profile to compute body composition.

adopt.title: Adopt existing slot
adopt.description: Use a slot whose consent code you know, for example one Home Assistant created before a reinstall. Don't adopt a scale user that the Beurer app also uses: Home Assistant must be its only client.

data_description.person: Optional. Links the scale user to a Home Assistant person.
data_description.name: Leave empty to use the person's name.
data_description.slot: The slot number on the scale.
data_description.consent_code: The 4-digit code chosen when this scale user was created.

reconfigure.title: Change scale user
reconfigure.description: Renaming the scale user or changing its person doesn't need the scale. Changing the profile does: Home Assistant then asks you to wake the scale and writes the new profile to it.

data_description.person: Optional. Links the scale user to a Home Assistant person.
data_description.name: Leave empty to use the person's name.
data_description.birth_date: The scale supports ages from 10 to 100 years.

repair_create.title: Create the scale user again
repair_create.description: Home Assistant creates {name} on the scale again, with the stored profile and a new consent code. The scale may put the scale user into a different slot; its sensors stay the same. {name} then steps on the scale once and stays on until its display goes dark; that reading teaches the scale who they are.

progress.wake: Step on the scale to wake it. Home Assistant then connects, checks the consent code and reads the profile from the scale.
progress.create_wake: Step 1 of 3, connecting: the new scale user steps on the scale now and stays on until the display goes dark. That one step-on wakes the scale and teaches it who they are. Don't step off early.
progress.create_user: Step 2 of 3, creating the scale user: Home Assistant is creating the scale user on the scale and writing its profile. Keep standing on the scale.
progress.create_measure: Step 3 of 3, measuring: the scale is measuring. Stay on until it has shown all results and the display goes dark (the Bluetooth icon may stay lit). Wait for that before anyone steps on the scale again.
progress.reconfigure: Step on the scale to wake it. Home Assistant then connects and writes the new profile to the scale.

pairing_impossible.title: {name} can't pair through this Bluetooth path
pairing_impossible.description:
Home Assistant reached the scale {name}, but the Bluetooth adapter or proxy it used couldn't pair (bond) with it. The scale only stays connected when it is paired, so readings aren't synced.

To fix it, do one of these:
- Add an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy on an ESP32 near the scale. ESPHome proxies pair with the scale automatically.
- If Home Assistant uses its own Bluetooth adapter, make the host adapter pairable. A local adapter on Home Assistant OS usually can't pair.

If the scale was factory-reset, the adapter or proxy may still hold its old bond. Home Assistant removes that bond by itself on an ESPHome proxy. On a local adapter, remove the scale in the Bluetooth settings of the host (for example `bluetoothctl remove <address>`) and step on the scale again.

This issue goes away after the next successful sync.

unsupported_unit.title: {name} reports weights in {unit}
unsupported_unit.description:
The scale {name} sent readings in {unit} instead of kg. Home Assistant only supports kg and didn't record these readings, so your sensors don't show wrong values.

Set the scale's display unit back to kg, for example in the Beurer app. Home Assistant never changes the scale's settings. This warning goes away with the next reading in kg.

deletion_failing.title: {name}: removed scale users are still not deleted on the scale
deletion_failing.description:
The scale users in slot(s) {slots} were removed in Home Assistant, but {name} still has them: Home Assistant did not manage to delete them in the last {wakes} wakes of the scale. They keep taking up slots.

The likely causes are that Home Assistant never connects to the scale, or that the connection fails:
- Home Assistant scans passively. The scale's advertisements don't reach it in a way it can act on.
- The Bluetooth proxy is too far from the scale, or its connection is weak.
- The proxy or adapter holds an old bond with the scale, for example after a factory reset.

Check the **Pending deletions** sensor on the scale's device. Move the proxy closer to the scale and step on the scale again. This issue goes away when the deletions have run.

no_scan_response.title: {name}: Home Assistant sees no pending weigh-ins
no_scan_response.description:
The last {wakes} times {name} woke up, Home Assistant never received its scan response. The scale lists its pending weigh-ins only there, so Home Assistant can't tell who stepped on and doesn't sync them.

The Bluetooth path that hears the scale scans passively. Home Assistant asks for active scanning when the scale wakes, but not every path complies:
- ESPHome Bluetooth proxy: open the proxy's entry in Home Assistant, go to **Configure** and set **Bluetooth scanning mode** to **Active**.
- Home Assistant's own adapter: check that it supports active scanning.
- The proxy may be too far from the scale.

This issue goes away when a scan response arrives.

data_description.notify_unrecognised: Send a notification when someone steps on the scale and it recognises them as none of its scale users, so they can be added.

factory_reset.title: Factory reset the scale
factory_reset.description:
This deletes every scale user on the scale, including the ones the Beurer app or other clients use. It can't be undone. Home Assistant removes its own scale users as well, and removes the scale's old Bluetooth bond so the next connection pairs afresh. Their readings stay in Home Assistant's history.

Submit to continue; Home Assistant then asks you to step on the scale.

progress.factory_reset_wake: Step on the scale to wake it. Home Assistant then connects and resets it. Stay on the scale until the display goes dark.

abort.factory_reset_done: The scale was reset and its scale users are gone. Choose "Add scale user" on the scale's page to create the first one again.
abort.wake_timeout: The scale didn't wake up within 3 minutes. Nothing was changed. Start again and step on the scale.
abort.pairing_unsupported: The Bluetooth adapter or proxy that reached the scale can't pair with it, so nothing was changed. Use an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, or make the host adapter pairable. If the scale was factory-reset before, the path may still hold its old bond: Home Assistant can remove that only on an ESPHome proxy.
abort.cannot_connect: Home Assistant couldn't reset the scale. Make sure it is in range, then try again. If the display showed a reset, step on the scale again and add a scale user.
